issues.legal_issue: A final judgment in a bona fide public interest proceeding bars a later public interest proceeding from re-agitating issues decided, or issues that could and should have been raised, in the earlier proceeding.
material_facts: An earlier bona fide public interest proceeding challenged the project agreement, including the amount of land to be acquired and the allegation that the project concealed a real-estate venture.
The earlier court considered and rejected the challenge, including the claim that excessive land was being acquired, and its judgment became final.
A later public interest proceeding sought substantially similar relief against the same agreement and project, again raising the issue of excess land.
issues.conclusion: The earlier judgment operated as res judicata and barred the later challenge, including renewed arguments about excess land.
issues.legal_principle: Section 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, including Explanations III, IV and VI, recognises the general doctrine of res judicata. A bona fide public interest judgment binds the public at large, and the bar extends to matters that were decided or that could and ought to have been raised earlier. The Court relied on Forward Construction Co. v. Prabhat Mandal, Henderson v. Henderson, Greenhalgh v. Mallard, State of U.P. v. Nawab Hussain, and Direct Recruit, Class II Engineering Officers' Association v. State of Maharashtra.

rule.if: successive_public_interest_challenge and prior_public_litigation_bona_fide and prior_judgment_final and same_project_or_transaction_challenged and (issue_previously_decided or issue_could_and_should_have_been_raised)

predicates.successive_public_interest_challenge: A person brings a later public interest proceeding to challenge a project or transaction that was the subject of an earlier proceeding.
predicates.prior_public_litigation_bona_fide: The earlier public interest proceeding was brought bona fide to litigate a right held in common by the public.
predicates.prior_judgment_final: The judgment in the earlier proceeding became final.
predicates.same_project_or_transaction_challenged: The later proceeding challenges the same project or transaction as the earlier proceeding.
predicates.issue_previously_decided: The issue raised in the later proceeding was directly and substantially decided in the earlier proceeding.
predicates.issue_could_and_should_have_been_raised: The issue raised later belonged to the earlier dispute and could and ought to have been raised there.

issues.definition: When a bona fide public interest proceeding ends in a final judgment, a later challenge to the same project cannot re-open an issue already decided or one that could and should have been raised earlier.

issues.legal_issue: A claim that a public project agreement was procured by fraud or misrepresentation fails where the government knew of the relevant assignment and the agreement was extensively reviewed and approved.
material_facts: The consortium members assigned their project rights to a company and sent the assignment agreement to the government for consideration.
The government's law department advised that separate consent was unnecessary because the government was finalising an agreement with the assignee.
The draft project agreement was reviewed by government committees, modified, approved by the government, and then implemented for several years.
The government later alleged fraud and misrepresentation, but abandoned that argument before the Supreme Court; the Court agreed with the High Court that the allegation lacked substance.
issues.conclusion: There was no fraud or misrepresentation by the project company or the consortium members, and the later allegation did not undermine the agreement.
issues.legal_principle: The Court assessed the allegation against the record of the government's knowledge of the assignment and its deliberate review and approval of the agreement. It agreed with the High Court's finding that the fraud and misrepresentation plea was an afterthought and lacked bona fides; the State also expressly abandoned the contention before the Supreme Court.

rule.if: project_agreement_challenge_appeal and government_knew_of_assignment and agreement_reviewed_and_approved_by_government and fraud_contention_abandoned_on_appeal

predicates.project_agreement_challenge_appeal: An appeal challenges a judgment concerning the validity or implementation of a public project agreement.
predicates.government_knew_of_assignment: The government received information about the assignment of project rights before entering into its agreement with the assignee.
predicates.agreement_reviewed_and_approved_by_gover: Government bodies examined and approved the agreement before it was signed and implemented.
predicates.fraud_contention_abandoned_on_appeal: The government expressly gave up its fraud or misrepresentation contention in the appeal.

issues.definition: Where an appeal challenges a public project agreement, the government knew of the assignment, reviewed and approved the agreement, and abandoned its fraud contention, the alleged fraud or misrepresentation is not established.

issues.legal_issue: A constitutional court may direct a government to honour its project obligations where the government acts arbitrarily or with mala fides in exercising contractual rights, notwithstanding the contractual character of the dispute.
material_facts: The government was a party to an agreement for a major public infrastructure project and had undertaken obligations to facilitate its implementation.
The agreement had been implemented for several years, and the project company had invested substantial sums and performed project-related work.
After a change in government, the government halted or impeded implementation and raised allegations that the Court found to be unsupported and mala fide.
The High Court directed the government and its instrumentalities to implement the agreement and project in accordance with their commitments.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was entitled to direct implementation of the project agreement; the government remained obliged to exercise its contractual rights fairly, reasonably, and without mala fides.
issues.legal_principle: A State or its instrumentality remains subject to constitutional obligations when acting in a contractual capacity. Under Articles 12 and 226 of the Constitution, arbitrary or mala fide State action may be reviewed and appropriate relief may include a direction to perform a public or statutory obligation. The Court relied on Gujarat State Financial Corporation v. Lotus Hotels Pvt. Ltd., Kumari Shrilekha Vidyarthi v. State of U.P., Dwarkadas Marfatia and Sons v. Board of Trustees of the Port of Bombay, and Biman Krishna Bose v. United India Insurance Co. Ltd.

predicates.constitutional_writ_review_of_state_cont: A constitutional writ proceeding challenges a government's conduct in carrying out or exercising rights under a contract.
predicates.state_party_to_public_project_agreement: The government is a party to an agreement for a public project.
predicates.substantial_performance_or_reliance_unde: The agreement has been acted on through substantial performance, investment, or reliance by a contracting party.
predicates.state_action_arbitrary_or_mala_fide: The government has acted arbitrarily or with mala fides in exercising its contractual rights or carrying out its obligations.

issues.definition: A court may direct a government to honour a public project agreement when the government is a party to it, substantial performance or reliance has occurred, and its conduct is arbitrary or mala fide.

issues.legal_issue: A succeeding government must continue an unfinished, non-political public project adopted through consensus rather than discontinue it merely because the government has changed.
material_facts: A major public project had been adopted and was being implemented through a government agreement.
The project remained unfinished when the government changed.
The succeeding government halted or reconsidered the project, although the decision to implement it did not depend on a political philosophy.
issues.conclusion: A change of government alone did not justify stopping the project; the succeeding government was duty-bound to continue the unfinished work.
issues.legal_principle: The Court relied on State of U.P. v. Johri Mal and State of Haryana v. State of Punjab, which establish that a succeeding government must carry forward an unfinished decision based on consensus where it does not involve a political philosophy.

rule.if: unfinished_public_project and government_change and project_decision_based_on_consensus and project_does_not_involve_political_philosophy

predicates.unfinished_public_project: A public project adopted by the government remains incomplete.
predicates.government_change: A new government succeeds the government that adopted the project.
predicates.project_decision_based_on_consensus: The decision to undertake the project was based on consensus.
predicates.project_does_not_involve_political_philo: The project decision does not depend on a political philosophy.

issues.definition: When a government changes while a consensus-based, non-political public project remains unfinished, the succeeding government must continue it.

issues.legal_issue: A land acquisition challenge fails on the ground of non-service where the landowners were in fact served with notice and had an opportunity to object.
material_facts: The landowners challenged acquisitions under the applicable industrial development law, alleging that the required notice had not been served.
The lower courts found that the landowners had been served and had filed objections, and that finding was not successfully disputed before the Supreme Court.
issues.conclusion: The Court rejected the claim that the required acquisition notices had not been served.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied Section 28(1) of the Karnataka Industrial Areas Development Act, 1966, and relied on the concurrent factual findings that notice had been served and objections had been filed.

predicates.land_acquisition_appeal: An appeal challenges the validity of a land acquisition.
predicates.acquisition_notice_actually_served: The landowners were in fact served with the acquisition notice.
predicates.landowners_had_opportunity_to_object: The landowners had an opportunity to file objections to the proposed acquisition.

issues.definition: In a land acquisition appeal, a non-service challenge fails when notice was in fact served and the landowners had an opportunity to object.

issues.legal_issue: An acquisition notification is not invalid for vagueness where it identifies a sufficiently precise public purpose and the landowners can make and have their objections considered.
material_facts: The acquisition notifications stated that the land was being acquired for industrial development, including the establishment and development of industrial areas.
The acquisition covered a large area for a project with multiple connected components.
The landowners filed objections and the competent authority considered them after giving an opportunity to object.
The Court found no prejudice from the wording of the notifications.
issues.conclusion: The stated purpose was sufficiently precise, and the notifications were not invalid for vagueness or breach of natural justice.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied Sections 28(1) and 28(2) of the Karnataka Industrial Areas Development Act, 1966, and the principles of natural justice. It relied on Aflatoon v. Lt. Governor of Delhi, which explains that the precision required of a stated purpose depends on the circumstances and that a large acquisition may properly state the purpose by reference to the acquisition as a whole.

rule.if: land_acquisition_appeal and large_area_acquisition and notification_states_sufficiently_precise_public_purpose and landowners_can_object and objections_considered and no_material_prejudice_from_wording

predicates.land_acquisition_appeal: An appeal challenges the validity of a land acquisition notification.
predicates.large_area_acquisition: The acquisition covers a large area, potentially comprising land belonging to different owners.
predicates.notification_states_sufficiently_precise: The notification identifies a public purpose with sufficient precision in the circumstances of the acquisition.
predicates.landowners_can_object: The landowners have a meaningful opportunity to object to the proposed acquisition.
predicates.objections_considered: The competent authority considers the landowners' objections after giving them an opportunity to present them.
predicates.no_material_prejudice_from_wording: The wording of the notification does not materially prejudice the landowners' ability to object.

issues.definition: A notification for a large acquisition is not invalid for vagueness when it states a sufficiently precise public purpose, permits objections, and causes no material prejudice.

issues.legal_issue: Land situated away from a project's main road alignment may be acquired for a public purpose when it forms part of an integrated infrastructure project and falls within the applicable industrial development law.
material_facts: The project was conceived as an integrated infrastructure development project, including roads, interchanges, peripheral connections, and other infrastructure, rather than solely as a highway.
The land acquisition included land away from the main road alignment for connected project components, including township and infrastructure development.
The applicable law's definitions of industrial areas and industrial infrastructural facilities had been broadened to encompass infrastructure contributing to industrial development.
issues.conclusion: The acquisition of the entire land for the integrated project was for a public purpose and was within the acquisition powers of the applicable industrial development law, even where land was away from the main road alignment.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the Karnataka Industrial Areas Development Act, 1966, including Sections 2(6) and 2(7-a), as amended, and the State's power of eminent domain. It held that the statutory definitions encompassed infrastructure contributing to industrial development and that land for connected components of an integrated project need not lie on the main road alignment.

predicates.land_acquisition_appeal: An appeal challenges the acquisition of land for a public project.
predicates.acquisition_for_integrated_infrastructur: The land is acquired for a project comprising connected infrastructure components rather than a single road alone.
predicates.acquired_land_connected_to_project_compo: The acquired land, including land away from the main route, is connected to components of the integrated project.
predicates.statutory_industrial_infrastructure_scop: The applicable industrial development law covers the project's infrastructure and related facilities.

issues.definition: Land connected to an integrated infrastructure project may be acquired for a public purpose under the applicable industrial development law even when it lies away from the main route.

issues.legal_issue: A writ petition challenging an acquisition is not maintainable where the petitioners had no right or interest in the land when they filed it and cannot alter that position on appeal.
material_facts: In a set of acquisition proceedings, the High Court recorded that the petitioners had no right or interest in the relevant land when they filed their writ petitions.
Their counsel admitted that position before the High Court.
The petitioners could not establish a basis for taking a different position before the Supreme Court.
issues.conclusion: The writ petitions were not maintainable, and the High Court was justified in dismissing them on that basis.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the rule that an appellant cannot depart from the position on which the case proceeded below where that position was admitted, and upheld the conclusion that a petitioner without a right or interest in the land at filing could not maintain the writ petition.

rule.if: land_acquisition_appeal and petitioner_lacked_land_right_or_interest_when_filing and lack_of_interest_admitted_below and no_basis_for_changing_position_on_appeal

predicates.land_acquisition_appeal: An appeal concerns a writ petition challenging a land acquisition.
predicates.petitioner_lacked_land_right_or_interest: The petitioner had no right or interest in the land when the writ petition was filed.
predicates.lack_of_interest_admitted_below: The petitioner or counsel admitted the lack of a right or interest before the lower court.
predicates.no_basis_for_changing_position_on_appeal: The petitioner has no sufficient basis to take a different position on appeal.

issues.definition: A land acquisition writ petition is not maintainable when the petitioner lacked an interest in the land at filing, admitted that fact below, and cannot justify changing position on appeal.
